supplementaryReferences.title: Leaf vegetable identity and warm-climate culture
supplementaryReferences.note: Florida extension confirms Malabar spinach as a warm-climate leaf vegetable. Its Florida planting and harvest calendar is not a South African calendar.

supplementaryReferences.doc: UF/IFAS: Cultivation of Malabar Spinach in Florida
supplementaryReferences.note: Foreign extension reference for support, seed/cutting propagation and warm, moist conditions; no Florida months are imported into the South African plan.

supplementaryReferences.title: Optimal from-seed cutting-cycle reference — Florida extension
supplementaryReferences.quote: around 70 days from seed in optimal conditions
supplementaryReferences.doc: UF/IFAS: Florida Cultivation Guide for Malabar Spinach, Harvest and Storage
supplementaryReferences.note: The extension guide reports maturity around 70 days from seed under optimal conditions, followed by hand trimming leaves and young stems. This foreign optimal-condition duration is supplementary; no South African planting date, exact month window or generic tree-age value is inferred.

care: Provide climbing support and adequate moisture in a warm growing position.
Record successive leaf harvests by planting batch rather than using tree-age production.
purchase: Obtain labelled Basella alba material. A South African regional cultivar, kg/plant benchmark and dated picking window remain unverified.
